correctness.rationale: After positive diagonal scaling, the first two SOR sweeps reduce to \(Q_2=\omega[R+(1-\omega)R^2+\omega RUR]\) with \(R=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\omega^jL^j\). The exact identity \(R^2=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}(j+1)\omega^jL^j\) makes every coefficient nonnegative exactly through \(\omega=(n+1)/n\). Above that boundary, the explicit SPD tridiagonal chain has endpoint entry \(\omega^n\varepsilon^{n-1}[(n+1)-n\omega+(n-1)\omega^2\varepsilon^2]\), which is negative for sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\). Exact-rational replay confirms the stated \(n=3\) witness. The finite checker is supplementary; the proof covers arbitrary \(n\).

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete, dimension-explicit finite-horizon safety law for a canonical overrelaxed solver: the amount of universally safe overrelaxation at sweep two is exactly \(1/n\). This directly separates asymptotic SOR convergence from order-cone preservation and provides a sharp diagnostic for positivity-sensitive inverse-positive systems. The chain witness shows the boundary is structural, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
